THE GOVERNMENT SAVINGS BANKS ACT, 1873
THE GOVERNMENT SAVINGS BANKS ACT, 1873
ACT No. V of
1873
[28th January, 1873]
An Act to amend the law
relating to Government Savings Banks.
[For the
Statement of Objects and Reasons to the Bill, which was based upon the Trustee
Savings Banks Act, 1863 (26 and 27 Vict., c. 87), s. 30, see Gazette of India,
1872 Pt. V, p. 575 ; for Proceedings in Council, see ibid,, 1872, Supplement,
pp. 727, 743 ; ibid., 1873, Supplement, pp. 150 and 221.
This Act
has been applied to the Chittagong Hill‑tracts with certain modi fications,
see Bengal Regulation III of 1944.
This Act
has been applied‑
(i) to
Baluchistan, see the Baluchistan Laws Regulations, 1913 (Bal. Reg. 2 of 1913),
s. 3 ;
(ii) to
the Leased Areas of Baluchistan, see the Leased Areas (Laws) Order, 1950 (G. G.
O. 3 of 1950) ;
(iii) in
the Federated Areas of Baluchistan, see Gazette of India, 193.7. Pt. I, p.
1499.
It has
also been extended to‑
(a) the
Baluchistan States Union, see the Baluchistan States Union (Federal Laws)
(Extension) Order, 1953 (G. G. O. 4 of 1953) , as amended ;
(b) the
Khairpur State, see the Khairpur (Federal Laws) (Extension) Order, 1953 (G. G.
O. 5 of 1953), as amended.
The Act
has been and shall be deemed to has been brought into force in t6wadur (with
effect from the 8th September, 1958), by the Gwadur (Appli cation of Central
Laws) Ordinance, 1960 (37 of 1960), s. 2.]
PRELIMINARY
1.Short title. This Act
may be called the Government Savings Banks Act, 1873.
[Local extent. It extends
to the whole of Pakistan.] [See foot‑note 2 on
page 1.47, supra.]
[Commencement
clause rep. by the Repealing Act, 1874 (16 of 1874).]

[Repeal of Act XXVI of 1855.]

PRELIMINARY
3. Interpretation clause.
In this Act‑
" depositor " means a
person by whom, or on whose behalf, money has been heretofore, or shall be
hereafter, deposited in a Government Savings Bank ; and "deposit"
means money so deposited
[Subs. by
the Govt. Savings Banks (Amdt.) Act, 1923 (16 of 1923), s. 2, for the original
definition.]["Secretary" means, in the case of a Post Office
Savings Bank, the Postmaster‑General appointed for the area in which the
Savings Bank is situate [Ins. by A. O., 1949, Sch.]
[or if that area is in India, [The word "by"
rep. by the Federal Laws (Revision and Declaration) Act, 1951, (26 of 1951), s.
3 and II Sch.] the Postmaster‑General for such area in Pakistan as
the Central Government may by general or special order specify in this behalf
:]
[Subs. by
the Amending Act, 1916 (13 of 1916), s. 2 and Sch., for the original definition.]
["minor" means a person who is not deemed to have attained his
majority under the Majority Act, 1875.](IX of 1875.)

Payment of death of depositor

DEPOSITS BELONGING TO THE ESTATES OF DECEASED
PERSONS
4.Payment of death of
depositor. [This section was subs. first by the
Govt. Savings Banks (Arndt.) Act, 1923 (16 of 1923), s. 3 and then by the Govt.
Savings Banks (Amdt.) Act, 1943 (2 of 1943), s. 2, to read as above.] If
a depositor dies and probate of his will or letters of administration of his
estate or a succession certificate granted under the Succession Act, 1925, is
not within three months of the death of the depositor produced to the Secretary
of the Govern ment Savings Bank in which the deposit is, then‑(XXXIX of
1925)
(a) if the deposit does not exceed
[Subs. by the Government Savings Bank and Securities
Laws (Amdt) Act, 1958 (42 of 1958), s. 2 and Sch., for "five thousand
rupees" (with effect from the 1st March, 1960).] [twenty‑five
thousand rupees], the Secretary may pay the same to any person appearing to him
to be entitled to receive it or to ad minister the estate of the deceased, and
(b) within the aforesaid limit of
[Subs. by the Government Savings Bank and Securities
Laws (Amdt) Act, 1958 (42 of 1958), s. 2 and Sch., for "five thousand
rupees" (with effect from the 1st March, 1960).] [twenty‑five
thousand rupees], any officer employed 'in the management of a Government
Savings Bank who is empowered in this behalf by a general or special order of
the Central Government may, to the extent to which he is em powered by such
order and subject to any general or special orders of the Secretary in this
behalf, pay the deposit to any person appearing to him to be entitled to
receive it or to administer the estate.]

Payment to be a discharge

THE GOVERNMENT SAVINGS BANKS ACT, 1873
THE GOVERNMENT SAVINGS BANKS ACT, 1873
ACT No. V of
1873
[28th January, 1873]
An Act to amend the law
relating to Government Savings Banks.
DEPOSITS BELONGING TO THE ESTATES OF DECEASED
PERSONS
5.Payment to be a discharge.
Saving of right of executor. Saving right of creditor. Such payment shall
be a full discharge from all further liability in respect of the money so paid
But nothing herein contained
precludes any executor or ad ministrator, or other representative of the
deceased, from re covering from the person receiving the same the amount
remaining in his hands after deducting the amount of all debts or other demands
lawfully paid or discharged by him in due course of ad ministration.
And any creditor or claimant
against the estate of the de ceased may recover his debt or claim out of the
money paid under this Act or [The words "the
said" rep. by the Amending Act, 1891 (12 of 1891), s. 2 and Sch. I.]
Act No. XXVI of 1855 [Rep. by s. 2 of this Act.], to any
person, and remaining in his hands unadministered, in the same manner and to
the same extent as if the latter had obtained letters of adminis tration of the
estate of the deceased.

Security for due administration

THE GOVERNMENT SAVINGS BANKS ACT, 1873
THE GOVERNMENT SAVINGS BANKS ACT, 1873
ACT No. V of
1873
[28th January, 1873]
An Act to amend the law

6.Security for due
administration. The Secretary of any such Bank [Ins.
by the Govt. Savings Banks (Amdt. Act, 1923 (16 of 1923), s. 4.] [or any officer em powered under
section 4] may take such security as he thinks necessary from any person to
whom he pays any money under section 4 for the due administration of the money
so paid,
and he may assign the said
security to any person interested in, such administration.

Power to administer oath

THE GOVERNMENT SAVINGS BANKS ACT, 1873
THE GOVERNMENT SAVINGS BANKS ACT, 1873
ACT No. V of
1873
[28th January, 1873]
An Act to amend the law
relating to Government Savings Banks.
DEPOSITS BELONGING TO THE ESTATES OF DECEASED
PERSONS
7.Power to administer oath.
Penalty for false statements. For
the purpose of ascertaining the right of the person claiming to be entitled as
aforesaid, the Secretary of any such Bank [Ins. by the
Govt. Savings Banks (Amdt. Act, 1923 (16 of 1923), s. 4.] [or any officer empowered under
section 4] may take evi dence on oath or affirmation according to the law[See the Oaths Act, 1873 (10 of 1873).] for the time being relating to oaths and
affirmations.
Any person who, upon such oath or
affirmation, makes any statement which is false, and which he either knows or believes
to be false or does not believe to be true, shall be deemed guilty of an
offence under section 193 of the Pakistan Penal Code.(XLV of 1860)

Deposit when excluded in computing court-fees

THE GOVERNMENT SAVINGS BANKS ACT, 1873
THE GOVERNMENT SAVINGS BANKS ACT, 1873
ACT No. V of
1873
[28th January, 1873]
An Act to amend the law
relating to Government Savings Banks.
DEPOSITS BELONGING TO THE ESTATES OF DECEASED
PERSONS
8. Deposit when excluded in
computing court-fees. Where the amount of the deposit belonging to the
estate of a deceased depositor does not exceed
[Subs. by the Government Savings Banks (Amdt.)
Act, 1917 (17 o 1917), s. 2, for "one thousand rupees".]
[three thousand rupees,] such amount shall be excluded in computing the fee
chargeable, under the Court fees Act, 1870, on the probate, or letters of ad ministration,
or certificate ; if any), granted in respect of his pro perty[Cf. the Savings Bank Act, 1828 (9 Geo 4, c. 92), s. 40, now
rep. by the Savings Banks Act, 1863 (26 and 27 Vict., c. 87).]: (VII of
1870.)
Provided that the person claiming
such probate or letters or certificate shall exhibit to the Court authorized to
grant the same a certificate of the amount of the deposit in any Government Sav ings
Bank belonging to the estate of the deceased. Such certifi cate shall be signed
by the Secretary of such Bank, and the Court shall receive it as evidence of
the said amount.

Act not to apply to deposits belonging to estates of European soldiers or deserters

9.Act not to apply to deposits
belonging to estates of European soldiers or deserters. Nothing
hereinbefore contained applies to money belong ing to the estate of any
European officer, non‑commissioned officer or soldier dying in [Subs. by A. O., 1961, Art 2 and
Sch., for "Her Majesty's service" (with effect from the 23rd March,
1956).] [the service of the State] in [Subs. by
A. O., 1949, Sch., for "India".] [Pakistan], or of any
European who, at the time of his death, was a deserter from the said service.

Payment of deposits to minor or guardian

THE GOVERNMENT SAVINGS BANKS ACT, 1873
THE GOVERNMENT SAVINGS BANKS ACT, 1873
ACT No. V of
1873
[28th January, 1873]
An Act to amend the law
relating to Government Savings Banks.
DEPOSITS
BELONGING TO MINORS
10.Payment of deposits to
minor or guardian. Any deposit made by, or on behalf of, any minor may be
paid to him personally if he made the deposit, or to his guardian for his use
if the deposit was made by any person other than the minor, together with the
interest accrued thereon.
The receipt of any minor or
guardian for money paid to him under this section shall be a sufficient
discharge therefor.

Legalization of like payments heretofore made

THE GOVERNMENT SAVINGS BANKS ACT, 1873
THE GOVERNMENT SAVINGS BANKS ACT, 1873
ACT No. V of
1873
[28th January, 1873]
An Act to amend the law
relating to Government Savings Banks.
DEPOSITS
BELONGING TO MINORS
11.Legalization of like
payments heretofore made. All payments of deposits heretofore made to
minors or their guardians by any Secretary of a Government Savings Bank shall
be deemed to have been made in accordance with law.

Payment of deposits belonging to lunatics

THE GOVERNMENT SAVINGS BANKS ACT, 1873
THE GOVERNMENT SAVINGS BANKS ACT, 1873
ACT No. V of
1873
[28th January, 1873]
An Act to amend the law
relating to Government Savings Banks.
DEPOSITS BELONGING TO LUNATICS
12.Payment of deposits
belonging to lunatics. If any depositor becomes insane or otherwise
incapable of managing his affairs,
and if such insanity or
incapacity is proved to the satisfaction of the Secretary of the Bank in which
his deposit may be,
such Secretary may, from time to
time, make payments out of the deposit to any proper person,
and the receipt of such person,
for money paid under this section, shall be a sufficient discharge therefor.
Where a committee or manager of
the depositor's estate has been duly appointed, nothing in this section
authorizes payments to any person other than such committee or manager.

Payment of married women’s deposits

THE GOVERNMENT SAVINGS BANKS ACT, 1873
THE GOVERNMENT SAVINGS BANKS ACT, 1873
ACT No. V of
1873
[28th January, 1873]
An Act to amend the law
relating to Government Savings Banks.
Deposits made by Married Women
13.Payment of married women s
deposits. Any deposit made by or on behalf of a married woman, or by or on
behalf of a woman who afterwards marries, may be paid to her, whether or not
the Indian Succession Act, 1865[See now the Succession
Act, 1925 (39 of 1925).], section 4, applies to her marriage ; and her
receipt for money paid to her under this section shall be a sufficient
discharge therefor.(X of 1865.)

Rules regulating certificates under section 8, and payments under section 10, 12 or 13

THE GOVERNMENT SAVINGS BANKS ACT, 1873
THE GOVERNMENT SAVINGS BANKS ACT, 1873
ACT No. V of
1873
[28th January, 1873]
An Act to amend the law
relating to Government Savings Banks.
Rules
14.Rules regulating
certificates under section 8, and payments under section 10, 12 or 13. All
certificates under section 8; and all payments under section 10, section 12 or
section 13, shall be respectively granted and made by the Secretary of the
Bank, subject to such rules con sistent with this Act as the [Subs. by A. O., 1937, for "G. G. in C.".]
[Central Government] may, from time to time, prescribe[For
such rules, see Gazette of India, 1895, Pt. I, p. 406, and ibid., 1897,
Supplement, p. 158.].
